slides.say: Now a new question. A map has a scale of one to forty thousand. A lake covers five square centimeters on the map. What is the real area of the lake, in square kilometers?
So we know an area on the map, and we need the real area, in square kilometers. It's an area, so the scale will be squared.
Like in the lesson, first we change one map centimeter into kilometers. Forty thousand centimeters are four hundred meters, and four hundred meters are zero point four kilometers.
Now the area. One square centimeter on the map is a real square, zero point four kilometers by zero point four kilometers.
at: One square centimeter on the map

slides.say: Four times four is sixteen, so zero point four times zero point four is zero point one six square kilometers.
The lake is five square centimeters. Five times zero point one six is zero point eight. So the lake is zero point eight square kilometers.
at: Five times zero point one six

slides.say: Careful with two. That's five times zero point four, without squaring. And eight and zero point zero eight are one step of the decimal point away.
Choice number three is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
